learning_objectives: Identify the stem of a regular non-isc -ire verb by removing -ire.
Produce the six affirmative present indicative endings -o, -i, -e, -iamo, -ite and -ono.
Use checked non-isc -ire verbs in short present-time statements.

skills.description_en: Identify the stem of a regular non-isc -ire verb by removing -ire.
Recognise the six regular present indicative endings for non-isc -ire verbs.
Produce the correct regular non-isc -ire present form for a stated person and number.
Use regular non-isc -ire present forms in short present-time statements.
Produce short present-tense sentences with regular non-isc -ire verbs.

lesson.short_explanation_en: Regular non-isc -ire verbs form the present indicative by removing -ire and adding -o, -i, -e, -iamo, -ite or -ono. Not all -ire verbs follow this pattern: some use -isc- in selected persons, which is taught separately in the next topic.

rule_blocks.explanation_en: Remove -ire from the infinitive and add the ending that matches the subject.
usage_notes_en: The first three singular endings are -o, -i and -e.
Noi uses -iamo, voi uses -ite and loro uses -ono.
The checked verbs in this lesson do not insert -isc-.
common_errors_en: Do not use -ete for voi; non-isc -ire verbs use -ite.
Do not use -iscono for these verbs; that pattern belongs to the -isc- class.
Do not assume every -ire verb is non-isc.

rule_blocks.heading_en: Use the pattern with checked verbs
rule_blocks.explanation_en: Sentire, aprire, partire and dormire follow the non-isc pattern in the present indicative.
usage_notes_en: The subject is often omitted because the ending identifies the person.
This lesson only covers the present indicative forms shown here.
common_errors_en: Do not add -isc- to sentire, aprire, partire or dormire in these present forms.

contexts.setting_en: Anna and Marco talk at home about their morning and evening routines.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.translation_en: Yes, I sleep well. And you?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.target: Dormo bene. La mattina apro la finestra.
lines.translation_en: I sleep well. In the morning I open the window.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Io apro la porta e poi parto.
lines.translation_en: I open the door and then I leave.

focus_items.explanation_en: Dormi is dorm- plus the second-person singular ending -i.

contexts.setting_en: A short description of Anna and Marco before they leave home.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.target: Marco sente la musica in casa.
lines.translation_en: Marco hears the music at home.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.translation_en: In the evening they sleep well.

focus_items.explanation_en: Sente uses the regular third-person singular ending -e.
